chunk_list:
Third ARIADNA release-preparation session to approve internal version v2.2, close documentation and access controls and clearly separate its maintenance metrics from the official v2.1 results.

Andrés Beltrán: v2.2 adds explained abstention, one-dimension clarifications and the new conflicting-current-evidence reason. We must decide whether it is ready for internal release.
Tomás Leal: On the reserved maintenance set, it achieves 85.1 percent correct abstention, 8.4 percent unnecessary abstention and 69.3 percent accuracy on answerable questions.
Sergio Vidal: These figures do not come from the v2.1 test set and do not replace the official benchmark results: recall@10 of 79.5 percent, MRR of 0.638 and accuracy of 68.2 percent.
Lucía Navarro: Guide 1.3 contains five reasons, evidence rules, human review and twenty bilingual examples. Final agreement on reasonCode is 0.92.
Nuria Castaño: The v2.2 image is separated from v2.1 and experimental branches. The official test set remains encrypted and is not required to run abstention functions.
Clara Ibáñez: Documentation distinguishes stable release from maintenance, official results from supplementary analysis and public data from restricted sets.
Elena Martín: What was the result of the 16 November user evaluation?
Nuria Castaño: Eighty-nine percent understood the abstention reason, 85 percent identified when human review was required and average trust was 4.4 out of 5.
Andrés Beltrán: Do any blockers remain?
Sergio Vidal: Only minor wording and post-release follow-up actions. They do not affect the package.
Andrés Beltrán: ARIADNA v2.2 is approved for internal release on 1 December 2026. v2.1 remains the official evaluation snapshot; v2.2 is a maintenance and user-experience version.
Elena Martín: Approved. Every communication must preserve that distinction.
